title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In SL2(Z), or GL2(Z), the generators are rho = [[0,1],[-1,1]] and sigma = [[0,-1],[1,0]]. These are read off from the inverses written on the previous page; rho has order 6 and sigma has order 4. Their product is the unipotent element rho*sigma = [[1,0],[1,1]] = eps_1, the image of the loop around the cusp.

The 'équation des lacets' (32), [alpha,rho] = [beta,sigma] eps_1(mu-1), is the condition for alpha*rho*alpha^{-1} * beta*sigma*beta^{-1} = rho*sigma*eps_1^{mu-1} = eps_1^mu. In words: conjugate the two torsion generators separately, and require that their product becomes the mu-th power of the cusp loop. This is the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type condition, with mu playing the role of the cyclotomic exponent, for an endomorphism of the (profinite) modular group preserving conjugacy classes of torsion and inertia. Here Grothendieck studies it not in the discrete or profinite group but inside an algebraic group G: a twisted form of GL2 (the unit group of an Azumaya algebra M over S = Spec A), with a 1-parameter additive subgroup eps_1 : G_a -> SL(M).

This page:
- Specialisation. He takes G = GL(2)_Z and eps_1(lambda) = [[1,0],[lambda,1]], and notes eps_1(1) = rho*sigma. One checks rho*sigma = [[1,0],[1,1]]; correct.
- Viewpoint. Equation (32) is regarded as equations in the variables alpha, beta (local sections of G) and mu (a section of the affine line G_a). He announces that the hypotheses will force mu to lie in G_m.
- Reduction. Set xi = [alpha,rho] and eta = [beta,sigma]. Then det xi = det eta = 1, Tr(xi rho) = Tr(alpha rho alpha^{-1}) = Tr rho (= i, which is 1 here), and Tr(eta sigma) = Tr sigma (= j, which is 0 here). So he first studies the system xi = eta eps_1(mu-1), det xi = det eta = 1, Tr xi rho = i, Tr eta sigma = j.
- Lifting back. The previous page shows when such xi, eta come from some alpha, beta. One needs regularity: the discriminants D, resp. U, invertible. Solutions alpha, beta then exist with det = ±1, and in SL2 iff D ≡ 1 (3), resp. U ≡ 1 (4).
- Elimination. Since det eps_1 = 1, eta can be eliminated. The next page obtains three equations in (xi, mu): det xi = 1, Tr(xi rho) = Tr rho, and a third relation affine-linear in mu, P(xi) mu - Q(xi) = 0. It then uses eps_1 sigma = -lambda_0 rho, which with these matrices holds with lambda_0 = 1.

Purpose: understand the solution scheme of the loop equation, a GL2 'shadow' or linear representation of the GT-type equations, over general bases (e.g. Z_l), by reducing to conjugacy-class (trace/determinant) conditions on commutators.
errors: Equation numbers (33),(34),(35) are reused. They already label the homomorphism eps_1 on the previous page and formulas (34),(35) earlier on this page; this is a bookkeeping slip, not a mathematical error.
Minor: eta also satisfies det eta = 1 automatically once xi does, as noted in the NB. Hence (34) contains one redundant condition. Grothendieck notices this himself.

ideas.what: Reduce the loop equation [alpha,rho] = [beta,sigma] eps_1^{mu-1} to equations on the commutators xi, eta, using that a regular element of a form of GL2 is determined up to local conjugacy by its trace and determinant.
ideas.modern_name: Conjugacy classes of regular semisimple elements via characteristic polynomial; commutator/trace coordinates (character-variety style computation)

ideas.what: Treating the GT-type 'loop equation' for the modular group as an algebraic system over a base, in a twisted form of GL2 (Azumaya algebra) with a G_a-subgroup. Here mu is a variable on the affine line that is forced into G_m.
ideas.modern_name: Linear (GL2) image of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller relations / scheme of solutions of the GT equation in an algebraic group
ideas.usually_credited_to: GT theory: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; Lochak–Schneps for SL2 aspects
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche mention the action on the modular tower, but not this GL2 computation

ideas.what: Identification rho*sigma = [[1,0],[1,1]] = eps_1, the cusp loop as product of the order-6 and order-4 generators.
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (discussion of the modular group)

missed.claim: A systematic study of the 'équation des lacets' in an algebraic group setting: forms of GL2 attached to Azumaya algebras over Spec A, with mu a variable forced into G_m. The aim is to describe its solution scheme, e.g. over Z_l. This is a 'linearised' analogue of the profinite GT equations, and I do not know it to be worked out in the literature.
missed.quote: Nous considérons (32) comme des équations reliant les quantités locales variables α, β, μ — α, β sections locales de G, μ section de 𝔾_a — les hypothèses que nous allons faire impliquent d'ailleurs que μ sera en fait une section de 𝔾_m
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Explicit GL2 / l-adic images of GT-type equations relate to the l-adic representations of Galois on the modular tower and to the Ihara/Lochak–Schneps program. A solved algebraic model might give computable constraints on mu (cyclotomic character) and on the GT element's images.

deep.surprise_reason: Coherent, correct set-up computation in an unpublished line of thought (GT loop equation realised in GL2 over a base). The individual steps are routine linear algebra, and no finished non-trivial result appears on this page.
transcription_corrections: The underbrace label for Tr ρ is 'i' (with a vertical '=' sign), not 'τ'. This matches the next page's crossed-out 'posons i = Tr ρ, j = Tr σ'.
'435' at the top is Grothendieck's own page number, not part of the text.
The struck-out item before 'ρσ' in (35) is an erased symbol. The relation reads ε_1 = ε_1(1) = [[1,0],[1,1]] = ρσ.
'μ section de [crossed box]^1' is ambiguous. Possibly an affine line 𝔼^1 rather than 𝔾_a was written and then struck out.
